program_meta.program_name: TWO DISTINCT ROUTES - DO NOT CONFLATE. (1) MComp (Master of Computing, Computer Science Specialisation) - the standalone, application-based coursework master's. NUS Computing programme page, VERBATIM: 'Students admitted to the Master of Computing are required to pass 40 Units, and are given the flexibility to complete their programme by selecting one of the below options: Coursework Option [10 courses, no research] / CS Project Option [8 courses + a supervised project, 'sufficient practical and/or research experiences'] / CS Dissertation Option [6 courses + a supervised dissertation equivalent to 4 courses].' faculty.research_areas: Probabilistic & automated machine learning (Bayesian deep learning, Gaussian processes, Bayesian non-parametric models), data-efficient ML (Bayesian optimization, active learning, adaptive sampling, meta-learning), multi-party/federated/collaborative ML and data valuation, planning under uncertainty, multi-agent/robot systems.

His 'DAVINZ: Data Valuation using Deep Neural Networks at Initialization' (ICML 2022) and 'Validation Free and Replication Robust Volume-based Data Valuation' (NeurIPS 2021) build principled, cheap-to-compute criteria for exactly this decision, replacing the kind of manual threshold-tuning Akshat did by hand.
faculty.key_paper_1: DAVINZ: Data Valuation using Deep Neural Networks at Initialization. ICML, 2022.

(See also: Data Valuation in Machine Learning: 'Ingredients', Strategies, and Open Challenges, IJCAI 2022; Near-Optimal Task Selection for Meta-Learning with Mutual Information and Online Variational Bayesian Unlearning, AISTATS 2022.)

faculty.why_match: Akshat's core semi-supervised result rests on combining confidence thresholding with MC-dropout uncertainty to decide which pseudo-labels a teacher model's outputs can be trusted enough to train a student on. Soh's 'Refining Deep Generative Models via Discriminator Gradient Flow' (ICLR 2021) tackles the mirror problem on the generative side - using a learned discriminator signal to push generated samples toward the true data distribution rather than trusting the generator/discriminator at face value - which is conceptually the same move as Akshat's A-PDF filter (distrust the GAN discriminator, build an independent plausibility check instead). His more recent 'DiffPath' work (per a 2024 NUS Computing feature) on diffusion-based out-of-distribution detection extends this into the uncertainty-quantification-for-generative-models space directly relevant to interest (C).

faculty.research_areas: Deep learning theory and its interaction with practice: generalization bounds, optimization landscapes, diffusion model theory and sampling, mixup/calibration theory, large language models.
